title: - “Wonderful, Venerable Bharadvāja! Marvelous, Venerable Bharadvāja! This is well spoken by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.…
content: - “Wonderful, Venerable Bharadvāja! Marvelous, Venerable Bharadvāja! This is well spoken by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. This very cause, this very reason, Venerable Bharadvāja, is why these young monks, youthful, with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, do not indulge in sensual pleasures and live the perfectly pure holy life for their whole life, completing it fully. I too, Venerable Bharadvāja, when I enter the inner apartments with body unguarded, speech unguarded, mind unguarded, mindfulness unestablished, sense faculties unrestrained — then lust overcomes me. But, Venerable Bharadvāja, when I enter the inner apartments with body guarded, speech guarded, mind guarded, mindfulness established, sense faculties restrained — then lust does not overcome me.”

title: Elder Rāhula: Blinded by sensual desires, Covered by the net of wrong views, Craving acts as a veil, Covering, hiding completely. Bound by heedlessness, Like…
content:
Elder Rāhula:

Blinded by sensual desires,
Covered by the net of wrong views,
Craving acts as a veil,
Covering, hiding completely.
Bound by heedlessness,
Like a fish caught in a net.

I have overcome those sensual desires,
Cut Māra’s bondage.
Having pulled out the root of craving,
I am cooled, at peace.

title: “Carpenter, what are wholesome thoughts? Renunciation thought, non-ill-will thought, harmlessness thought. These, Carpenter, are called wholesome thoughts.”
content: “Carpenter, what are wholesome thoughts? Renunciation thought, non-ill-will thought, harmlessness thought. These, Carpenter, are called wholesome thoughts.”

title: “Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in them, praises…
content: “Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in them, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — because of that, delight arises. Migajāla, I say that with the arising of delight, suffering arises. Sounds … Odors … Tastes … Touches … Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind … If a monk delights in them, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — because of that, delight arises. Migajāla, I say that with the arising of delight, suffering arises.”

title: “Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and someone occasionally pours in oil and adjusts the wick —…
content: “Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and someone occasionally pours in oil and adjusts the wick — that oil lamp, being nourished and sustained in such a way, would burn for a long time. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are fetters — craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging arises … Thus the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and no one occasionally pours in oil or adjusts the wick — that oil lamp, being without its own fuel, with no further fuel added, not being nourished, would be extinguished. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing peril in things that are fetters — craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases … Thus the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing;…
content: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing; sounds cognizable by the ear … odors … tastes … touches cognizable by the body — desirable … enticing. These, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure. To abandon these five strands of sensual pleasure, monks, the four foundations of mindfulness should be developed.”

title: “Monks, here a monk, when there is sensual desire in him, knows: ‘There is sensual desire in me’; or when there is no sensual desire…
content: “Monks, here a monk, when there is sensual desire in him, knows: ‘There is sensual desire in me’; or when there is no sensual desire in him, knows: ‘There is no sensual desire in me.’ And he knows how unarisen sensual desire arises; he knows how arisen sensual desire is abandoned; and he knows how abandoned sensual desire does not arise in the future.”

title: “And what, monks, is the noble search? Here, monks, a person being himself subject to birth, having known the peril in what is subject to…
content: “And what, monks, is the noble search? Here, monks, a person being himself subject to birth, having known the peril in what is subject to birth, seeks the unborn, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to aging, having known the peril in aging, seeks the unaging, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna; being subject to sickness … the unailing … subject to death … the deathless … subject to sorrow … the sorrowless … subject to defilement, having known the peril in defilement, seeks the undefiled, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna. This, monks, is called the noble search.”

title: “Monks, if wanderers of other sects ask you: ‘For what purpose, friends, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?’ — being asked thus,…
content: “Monks, if wanderers of other sects ask you: ‘For what purpose, friends, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?’ — being asked thus, monks, you should answer them: ‘For the purpose of the destruction of greed, friends, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’ Then, monks, if they ask: ‘Is there, friends, a path, a way for the destruction of greed?’ — being asked thus, you should answer: ‘There is a path, a way for the destruction of greed.’ And what, monks, is that path, that way? It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view … right concentration. This, monks, is the path, the way for the destruction of greed. Being asked thus, monks, you should answer them in that way.”

title: “Then I, after some time, having known as they actually are the origination, the passing away, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in the…
content: “Then I, after some time, having known as they actually are the origination, the passing away, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in the case of sensual pleasures, abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, removed the fever for sensual pleasures, and dwelt with craving cut off, with mind inwardly peaceful. Then I saw other beings who had not abandoned lust for sensual pleasures being consumed by craving for sensual pleasures, being burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, indulging in sensual pleasures. I did not envy them, nor did I delight in that. Why is that? Because, Māgandiya, there is this pleasure and rapture, apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome states, and having attained the heavenly pleasure, I dwell delighting in that. I do not envy what is inferior, nor do I delight in that.”
